--- title: "Poisson regression scale validation and performance" jupyter: python3 --- phit's `fit_poisson_matrix()`, R `glm(poisson)`, and statsmodels `GLM` with the Poisson family fit identical simulated observations at four sizes. The [raw report](poisson-results.json) keeps every timing sample, machine and runtime versions, input hashes, numerical outputs, and differences from R. ## Methods | Item | Setting | | --- | --- | | Workloads | 1,000, 100,000, and 1,000,000 rows with 3 coefficients; 100,000 rows with 11 coefficients (counts include the intercept) | | Data | Simulated with NumPy seed `20261011` (see [Simulation and agreement](#simulation-and-agreement)); all runtimes read the same 17-significant-digit CSV | | Machine | AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX virtual machine, 2 cores, 7.8 GiB, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64) | | Builds | phit release build; runtime versions are printed below | | Threads | Common BLAS and OpenMP thread variables set to 1 | | Repetitions | One untimed warm-up, then five timed fits per worker; workers run separately and alternate order between cases | | Statistic | Median and minimum in-process wall-clock time | | Timed | One complete fit with every output materialized, including PHP input and output conversion | | Excluded | Startup, CSV loading, data generation, and JSON serialization | | Memory | Peak RSS of the whole worker process, from `peakmem` ([bench/peakmem.c](https://github.com/phpstats/phit/blob/main/bench/peakmem.c)) | The harness is shared with the [OLS benchmark](ols.qmd#timing-boundaries), which describes the boundaries in more detail. ## Recorded results ::: {#cd273b61 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path import json import pandas as pd # Keep display order independent of the benchmark worker execution order. def ordered_table(rows): table = pd.DataFrame(rows) table["implementation"] = pd.Categorical( table["implementation"], categories=["R", "statsmodels", "PHP"], ordered=True) return table.sort_values(["observations", "coefficients", "implementation"]).reset_index(drop=True) ROOT = next(p for p in [Path.cwd(), *Path.cwd().parents] if (p / "Cargo.toml").exists()) report = json.loads((ROOT / "docs/benchmarks/poisson-results.json").read_text()) assert report["model"] == "poisson" print("Recorded:", report["recorded_at"]) print("Machine:", report["cpu"], report["platform"]) print("Rust:", report["rust"]) print("Repeats:", report["repeats"], "Warm-ups:", report["warmups"]) rows, memory = [], [] for case in report["cases"]: assert case["agreement_passed"] for name, fit in case["implementations"].items(): rows.append({"observations": case["n"], "coefficients": case["p"], "implementation": name, "version": fit["version"], "median full fit (ms)": 1000*fit["median_fit_seconds"], "minimum full fit (ms)": 1000*fit["min_fit_seconds"]}) memory.append({"observations": case["n"], "coefficients": case["p"], "implementation": name, "CSV load (s)": fit["load_seconds"], "whole process (s)": fit["process_seconds"], "peak process RSS (MiB)": fit["peak_rss_bytes"]/2**20 if fit["peak_rss_bytes"] else None}) display(ordered_table(rows)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Recorded: 2026-11-01T19:43:27.332000+00:00 Machine: AMD Ryzen 9 9955HX 16-Core Processor Linux, Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS (x86_64) Rust: rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13) Repeats: 5 Warm-ups: 1 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

These measurements describe this workload on this machine. ## Visual comparison ::: {#53d56771 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` benchmarks/figures/poisson-fit-time.svg benchmarks/figures/poisson-memory.svg ``` ::: ::: ![Full-fit times for R, statsmodels and PHP in four workloads. Bars show median times; dots show individual repetitions.](figures/poisson-fit-time.svg) ![Peak whole-process memory for R, statsmodels and PHP in four workloads.](figures/poisson-memory.svg) Each panel has its own linear scale, so compare labeled values across panels. Download the timing [SVG](figures/poisson-fit-time.svg) or [PNG](figures/poisson-fit-time.png) and memory [SVG](figures/poisson-memory.svg) or [PNG](figures/poisson-memory.png). ## Timing boundaries Each timed fit materializes coefficients, covariance, standard errors, normal z tests, p-values, Wald intervals, every fitted mean count and response residual, likelihood, deviance, null deviance, AIC, and residual df. | Implementation | Fitting | | --- | --- | | phit | Weighted SVD Newton updates, with phit's convergence rules | | R | Formula and model construction, then QR-based IRLS with epsilon 1e-16 | | statsmodels | IRLS with parameter tolerance 1e-11 | Starting values, linear solves, and stopping criteria differ, so iteration counts differ too. This compares complete public API calls, not decomposition speed. ::: {#c946993c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} display(ordered_table(memory)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

PHP's `memory_limit` is disabled, because large nested PHP arrays can exceed typical application limits. ## Simulation and agreement After the common benchmark setup, visitor counts are integers uniform from 80 to 300, and staffing is visitors/50 plus normal noise with standard deviation 0.8, clipped. The wider case adds independent standard-normal scores. Outcomes are draws from $$\mu_i=\exp(0.1+0.005\,\mathrm{visitors}_i-0.12\,\mathrm{staff}_i +0.1\sum_j\mathrm{extra}_{ij}),\qquad y_i\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\mu_i).$$ This simulation is separate from the small teaching sample. Data hashes, generating coefficients, and sample correlations are recorded. Coefficient-level quantities and scalar statistics are compared with R at `1e-9 + 1e-7 * abs(reference)`. Fitted values and residuals are computed in full and compared at ten evenly spaced rows; the small fixtures compare full vectors. phit must report convergence within 1 to 100 updates. Wald intervals follow R `confint.default()`, and the null baseline follows the documented intercept convention. Poisson deviance uses the saturated count likelihood, not −2 log-likelihood. ::: {#37c38bb2 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} display(ordered_table([{ "observations": case["n"], "coefficients": case["p"], "implementation": name, "largest absolute difference vs R": max(errors.values())} for case in report["cases"] for name, errors in case["max_absolute_errors_vs_R"].items()])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Reproduction ```sh cargo build -p phit --release --locked .context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/benchmarks/run.py --model poisson QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python" \ quarto render docs/benchmarks/poisson.qmd ``` Set matching `PHP` and `PHP_CONFIG`, and use `.so` on Linux. For a quick check that leaves the published report unchanged, add `--cases 1000:3 --repeats 2 --output .context/poisson-smoke.json`. A numerical failure aborts the run without writing results.
